Hand this letter to the Claw of Harvest Den.  
  
---    
    
I write with urgency, Alder. We have finally revealed the source of the blight, and what a monstrous sight it is. A stranger has become one with an abandoned city—a city that somehow eluded us all these years. The sky watchers say that it was shielded by a ward of some type, which kept the city hidden from the naked eye.   
  
The stranger was left within this ward and, as we've witnessed with the others, adapted to its habitat. It lingered for many lifetimes. It grew and consumed until it became unlike the three we hunted on the thundering isle. Although it seems petrified by stone, this one's maw alone could consume all of the den in a single bite. The smell... It's worse than a rotted corpse; sickly sweet and sour. The smell penetrates everything around us.  
  
The sky watchers say that to defeat it, we must destroy its organs. As the body is so large, there is simply no other advantage, and until the organs have been stilled, it continues to regenerate its life-fire. I admit that I am conflicted by the brutality of this, but there seems to be no other way.  
  
While we fight back against the body, the wayfinder's party is seeking to shut a poisonous gate at the heart of the city. This gate is feeding the stranger, somehow, giving it even more power. I raise my spear, nonetheless.  
  
I encourage you to hold firm at home. If circumstances were to collapse here, our people will need their leader.

Having reached the gates of Lion's Arch, the duchess and her attaché were finally granted entry into the city. They were escorted to the palace by the Lionguard; it was "a humid evening, despite the coastal breeze." Even at that hour, King Jadon was engaged in council with his advisors as charr forces amassed on the eastern Krytan border. Duchess Adelaide presented the king with the diplomatic parcel as he made introductions. When King Jadon addressed the emissary from the White Mantle, the duchess noticed three imposing figures garbed in golden robes and armor, with multiple sets of dark ethereal wings emerging from their backs. They hovered quietly, flanking the "stout but stern man in unusually vibrant attire" in a corner of the inner chamber.  
  
Unknown to most, the duchess was in possession of a relic stolen from Orr early in the Third Guild War. The Veil of Ilya, an elegant but otherwise visibly unremarkable domino mask, was rumored to pierce the curtain of reality, to look upon things not normally seen by mortal eyes. Its passive magic would allow the wearer to perceive things hidden by illusion or that exist out of phase with Tyria proper as if they were there normally. Should the wearer actively draw upon the Veil's well of power, they may reveal these things to those around them within a defined space and for a short period of time.  
  
Before the Unseen could act, the duchess exposed them with the full power of the Veil. It was said that the mursaat attacked with powerful magics, killing the king's advisors and royal guard in seconds. Adelaide and her companions came to the king's defense with combined feedback spells, evacuating His Royal Highness through secret corridors at his direction.

283, Colossus, 1076 AE  
  
No sooner had the ink on my writ of exaltation dried than I was granted an audience with our hosts in the holy city. My unwavering faith has been rewarded at last. The last of my doubts, washed clean from my eyes. The Unseen were a marvel to behold. Regal, daunting, and beyond comprehension. Their words hang on the ear as honey on a spoon. Eloquence matched only by their golden visages.  
  
I must prove myself indispensable—to our gods and to the twins! I will not fall short of the mark, caught out as my predecessor was. The Eye sees only two kinds of sacrifices: the Chosen—those bright souls destined for greater purpose—and the disgraced, who've failed to carry out the will of our gods and are found wanting.  
  
My former teacher, Inquisitor Adin, will be executed on the stone tomorrow. May his spirit do more for our saviors in death than his efforts amounted to in life.
